claims.claim: CPSO's board approved amendments on Oct. 13, 2026 requiring physicians to identify 'safer supply' and specify 'no carries' on prescriptions, supporting supervised consumption
claims.attributed_to: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario

claims.claim: The amendments require safer supply be prescribed only with opioid agonist therapy and an in-person assessment at least monthly
claims.attributed_to: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario

claims.claim: CPSO expects transition to compliance by Nov. 16, 2026
claims.attributed_to: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario

claims.claim: An eight-week prescribing time limit previously considered was not included in the approved changes
claims.attributed_to: The Globe and Mail / The Canadian Press

claims.claim: CPSO says the amendments do not prohibit safer supply prescribing
claims.attributed_to: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario

claims.claim: The board heard information from governments and medical groups that hydromorphone diversion is occurring, but no data quantifies how much street supply comes from safer supply prescriptions
claims.attributed_to: Dr. Anil Chopra, CPSO associate registrar

claims.claim: Board member Peter Wiesner said more than 87 per cent of safer supply patients are also on OAT and raised concerns about the remaining 12 per cent, rural and employed patients
claims.attributed_to: Peter Wiesner, CPSO board member

claims.claim: North Bay police say the changes will 'pretty much eliminate diversion' and describe an attendance-based program
claims.attributed_to: Brad Reaume, North Bay Police Service

claims.claim: Ontario's Community Care and Recovery Act, 2024 sets a 200-metre restriction on injection sites near schools and requires provincial approval before municipalities seek federal exemptions or funding for supervised consumption or safer supply
claims.attributed_to: Ontario government

claims.claim: CPSO's proposal was reported Oct. 6, 2026, a week before the board vote, and builds on changes introduced in May 2026
claims.attributed_to: The Canadian Press

claims.claim: No data establishes the clinical or diversion effect of the supervised-consumption requirement
